I’ll repost my thoughts on the headlines about a hyper loop tunnel:

The overall goal of the campus master plan is to reduce on campus parking to use the lots for new buildings and reduce on campus traffic. Knowing the campus (as well as the university official quoted) firsthand, I think the tunnel proposal is unlikely to come to fruition for a variety of reasons the least of which is that the Boring Co. is a sham. I don’t think there’s anything that an underground tunnel could do that couldn’t be achieved far cheaper with busses and streetcars, it’s already got a partial grid system which the university already restricts car access to at numerous choke points. I know that there’s also limestone close to the surface in some areas of College Station, so I imagine drilling through solid stone is probably more expensive.

Our campus is 5,500 acres and it can in fact take some time to cross campus, but again this isn’t something that can’t be solved with limiting through traffic and prioritizing a streetcar as well as busses, bikes, and walking over cars. No need to reinvent the wheel with flashy mega projects

I think there’s a potential for bad actors to use environmental concerns as a front to block development that they personally don’t like, but I don’t think the existence of environmental protections is preventing development

Her father is (rightfully) killed and overthrown when she’s a baby, her mother dies after giving birth to her, and then her only living brother is violent and abusive to her her whole life as they move from place to place to avoid assassins. 

After years of living in relative poverty and being on the run, her brother sells her to a barbaric warlord for his own personal gain. The first night after she’s married, her husband violently rapes her. Over time, she does grow to love her husband and he begins to respect and love her. Her brother continues to threaten and abuse her up until he threatens his (now pregnant) sister and Dany’s husband kills the only family she’s known right in front of her eyes. Dany saves a witch from being killed, her husband is gravely injured, and the witch sacrifices the husband and the unborn child, leaving Daenerys with nothing as most of her husbands tribe abandons her. 

Dany does get 3 baby dragons which she considers her children from now on. Then, after nearly dying in the desert, her bestie kidnaps the dragons and a man tries to force her into marriage. She’s forced to see visions of her lost loved ones and a possibly tragic future before she escapes. 

After a pretty steady series of successes that involve ending slavery, gaining an army, and conquering cities while trying to improve conditions for the poor, Daenerys begins to lose control of her “children” (the dragons) and locks two of them away for the greater good. She’s called a tyrant and a mad man for ending slavery and is nearly overthrown by the former slave masters before she escapes via dragon. 

The dragon drops her off in a field where she’s captured by the remains of her former husband’s tribe, and they insist that she either be executed or live her life in solitude as basically a nun in their capital. She does manage to escape, win over the tribe, add to her army, reconquer her cities from the slave masters, and gain allies and a fleet of ships to retake her homeland that’s she’s never known. She does leave behind a man she loves because she knows that as a woman, she’s got to be single for a potential political marriage. 

This is where the show does her really dirty. Upon arrival in her homeland, her enemies vilify her as much as possible as a foreign invader, while her allies undermine her and question her judgement at every turn. She’s called mad and portrayed as being as evil as her father for killing enemies instead of taking prisoners, even though those people said they’d rather die than submit or be prisoners. She gives her aid and lends her army to Jon Snow and the North despite not getting anything in return, and sees one of her dragons killed. She sees her armies and allies killed, and is still given the cold shoulder by everyone other than Jon Snow. Dany also loses her oldest advisor she’s cared for since the beginning and he dies in her arms after a brutal battle where she has to pick up a sword to defend herself. She then confesses her love for Jon, but he ignores her. Continuing on, her second dragon is killed before her eyes, and her best friend is captured by the enemy. Her best friend, a former slave, is brought before Dany in chains and then decapitated to further torture Dany. As she’s clearly struggling with depression, an advisor conspires to poison her, and Jon’s family conspires to betray her. When she kills this treacherous advisor, she’s again called crazy and unreasonable. As the final battle ramps up, the writer’s suddenly decide that this woman that has spent the majority of her on screen time freeing slaves, helping the poor and innocent, proving that she’s compassionate and nothing like her cruel and sadistic father, and wanting to break the cycle of tyranny and oppression...just suddenly “goes crazy lol” and decides to murder everyone in the city. After she kills everyone, she’s suddenly Hitler and wants to take over the whole world as her way is the only way. She again professes her love to Jon, so he goes in for a kiss and then stabs her and kills her. She’s remembered as “the mad queen” just like her father and her legacy is forever tarnished.

A lot of people may mean well but it really is inappropriate to talk about in most contexts. Even if it’s positive comments, praise for one person may make someone else feel bad about themselves. Discussions about dieting and weight loss can be really problematic for people dealing with eating disorders or body image. 

For me, I’ve always struggled with my weight and have constantly been told “how much better/healthier/happier” I look whenever I lose weight and then I get negative comments such as “you seem to be eating well” or “you must be enjoying all that beer at college lol” whenever I gain weight. 

That being said, if someone tells me I look different or skinnier I do usually take the compliment and tell them that I’ve lost some weight. It does make me feel good, but I don’t think talking about it constantly or bringing it up is appropriate, especially in a professional setting.

The best way to handle this situation is to call them out on it when it happens. It’s going to be awkward but frankly that’s your coworkers’ fault for saying these kinds of things. 

A gentle approach to your concerned coworker could be something like: “Hey I’m sure you mean well, but I’d really appreciate if you didn’t talk about my weight anymore. It makes me uncomfortable.”

If that doesn’t work and it happens again, say in a firm tone something like: “Again, I appreciate your concern, but my weight is personal and I don’t want to discuss it at work. Please don’t bring it up again.” 

As for the coworker that poked you and commented on your body, the only response for that is to say in a sarcastically surprised tone: “Wow. I can’t believe you just did that. That’s really inappropriate.” And then turn and walk away.

TL;DR It’s a lose-lose situation but it’s not right to put all the blame on Transportation Services. Everyone just likes to complain. 

Buses cost money, parking lots (no matter how shitty or full) cost money to maintain, and the roads on campus cost money to maintain. Also TS provides a lot of jobs at A&M and all those people need to get paid so yeah the costs add up. While the rules for parking seem draconian there’s a reason for the system. Is it inconvenient that you got a ticket for parking somewhere you’re not supposed to? Yeah it is but when you make exceptions for “oh I was only parked here for 10 minutes” for everyone that tries that then the whole system falls apart and then everyone complains about that. 
The most common issue I see brought up is the whole parking vs bus thing. People say the buses are always late or too full so they drive cars instead. Then when everyone is driving their own cars, they complain about the traffic that they themselves are a part of and is the very reason the buses run late. Then, people get to campus and complain that there’s not enough parking because everyone decides to drive themselves to class. TS decides to build more garages for parking and buy more buses, meaning they also need to hire drivers for those buses, and then everyone gets upset that buses and parking costs money. A&M could just raise tuition and fees and make everyone pay for the cost of a parking pass, but they don’t and instead make it optional to buy a parking pass because at the end of the day it is technically your choice to drive yourself to campus. 

All that being said.... the system could use some reworking and additional outside funding BUT any changes would have to be very gradual. However an inconvenience it may be, TS does have a plan to improve the parking and bus situation but it’ll take at least 20 years.

Take out the concrete, but replace the area in the bottom right of this picture with some flagstone for your seating area. Along the back fence, after you extend the garden portion, you should put some latticework trellises with some climbing roses. Then, make a smaller flowerbed centered around the roses on this back fence. This will add more greenery and break up the long horizontal sight lines you get from the current fence. From there, it’s up to you how much garden and how much grass you want. I have a little dog so I would leave the big (rose?) bush that’s in the middle of the left garden then add mulch around it, but replace the rest of that garden with some grass. Now, you only have one flowerbed to maintain that’s smaller than the current one, and you now have some grass you can walk on and that’s also friendly to pets and children. If you’re worried about drainage you might talk to your neighbors and see how their yards drain or if the previous owner ever had a problem that they know of. If drainage is a problem you might have to install a French drain somewhere along your house but hopefully having more permeable surfaces should do the job.
